objective: Compute, for every planned claim in this lab that will be decided by counting successes over a small number of cases, the tightest interval its planned sample size can produce, and identify the planned purchases whose intervals cannot exclude the belief they exist to test
rationale: This lab already has the measured symptom: an eight-case sample that could not pin an interval tighter than nothing to 97 percent. That is not a bad result, it is an arithmetic certainty of eight cases, and it was discovered after the eight cases were bought. The whole content of this item is that the same arithmetic is available BEFORE the purchase and nobody runs it. A band-containment verdict at three converged members, which the lab has a standing rule for, admits intervals so wide that no containment claim at that size can distinguish a good model from a coin. Naming which planned items are in that condition is the deliverable, and it is a cancellation generator rather than a new purchase. THE NULL, AND IT IS NOT FITTED: the exact binomial interval at the stated sample size, which is a mathematical object and is not estimated from any of this lab's data. THE IDENTITY TEST, owner rule W dash 2, ANSWERED AGAINST THIS ITEM'S OWN CENTRAL QUANTITY AND ANSWERED YES. The width of an exact binomial interval is derived BY CONSTRUCTION from the sample size and the success count and nothing else. It is an identity. It therefore MAY NOT BE GATED ON as evidence about the world, and this proposal does not gate on it: the width is reported, as a design calculation, exactly as a mesh cell count is reported. What is gated on instead is a procedural fact that is not an identity, namely whether a planned claim's record carries its achievable width at its planned sample size before the sample is bought. That fact is a property of the record and cannot be computed from the width. Making this distinction explicitly is half the value of the item, because the lab's own recorded burn was a correlation of 0.9742 that carried no information because its null sat pinned at unity and the accepted iterate satisfied the constraint to about one part in ten thousand million million. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM WHAT IS ALREADY FILED, checked record by record: the standing no-verdict-below-three rule sets a floor and does not price anything above it; the band-containment census counts the scoreable pairs the lab already owns, looking backwards. This item looks forward and attaches a number to a purchase that has not been made.
gate: ZERO COMPUTE. Deliverable is a table, one row per planned claim that will be decided by a success count, carrying: the planned sample size, the exact interval width achievable at the best case and at the worst case success count, the belief the claim exists to move, and a three-valued disposition. INFORMATIVE if the achievable interval excludes the belief's alternative at the planned size. UNDERPOWERED if it cannot, in which case the row names the sample size that would, and the item's recommendation is to re-size or cancel; a purchase that cannot change a belief at any outcome is the exact shape this lab has said must not be written. NOT APPLICABLE for planned claims not decided by a success count, listed rather than silently dropped. THE WIDTHS ARE REPORTED AND ARE NOT A GATE, per the identity answer above. The gate is the procedural one: from adoption, a proposal whose verdict is a success count over cases carries its achievable width, and one that does not is refused at intake with the missing row named. Falsifier for the whole item: if every planned claim turns out already informative at its planned size, the item closes having removed a doubt and having cancelled nothing, and that is reported as the finding rather than padded.
cost_basis: ZERO solver compute; the arithmetic is a closed-form interval over integers. Scored in agent tool calls: forecast 25, between this lab's bounded-question band of 2 to 5 and its build-and-verify band of 33 to 72, because enumerating the planned claims is a corpus read while the arithmetic itself is one script. Actual counted from the executing agent's transcript.
expected_knowledge_gain: THE DISCRIMINATING OUTCOME. If any planned claim is underpowered at its planned size, that purchase is known in advance to be uninformative and either grows or dies, and the core minutes it would have consumed are the measured saving. If none is, the lab learns that its sample sizes are already adequate and the standing worry about small samples is retired for the current queue, which is also a belief change. The outcome that moves nothing is the width table considered on its own, which is why it is reported and not gated on.
hard_criterion_note: Starts no flow case. Closed-form arithmetic plus a read of the planned queue.

The standing rule that a model-form band states a containment verdict only at three or more converged members, whose floor this item prices
The band-containment census proposal, which counts the scoreable pairs the lab already owns; this item is its forward-looking complement and does not duplicate it

launch_prompt: Precision floor pass. ZERO COMPUTE. Step 1: enumerate the planned claims in the queue whose verdict is a count of successes over cases, and state the frame of the enumeration. Step 2: compute exact binomial interval widths at each planned sample size, at both extreme success counts. Step 3: build the table with the three-valued disposition and, for every underpowered row, the size that would fix it. Step 4: state in the record, in one sentence, that the widths are an identity in the sample size and the success count and are therefore reported and not gated on. Do not adjust any existing pre-registration; if a row implies a threshold should move, say so and STOP, because that is Katie's call. Record your own tool call count.
